newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot propane mixed, eyes U.S. levels.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot propane mixed, eyes U.S. levels.

text.p: Canada spot propane prices were mixed in steady trade, with the western hub rising on crop drying demand in the U.S. Midwest, traders said on Thursday.
Players added, however, the Canadian market as a whole may see some downward movement following the Energy Information Administration's Wednesday report showing strong stocks builds in the U.S.
The Canadian markets are tightly tied with the U.S. hubs of Mont Belvieu, Texas, and Conway, Kansas.
In the Edmonton hub of western Canada, spot propane rose about 2.00 cents in the week to between 46.25 cents and 46.50 cents a gallon.
"There has been some strong demand on the Cochin pipeline to the Midwest for crop drying," said a trader.
In the Sarnia hub in the east, spot propane remained fairly steady at 52.50/53.25 cents as players stand back to watch how far Belvieu will fall following its 1.3 million build in stocks.
Meanwhile, Sarnia normal butane rose one cent to 50.00 cents on demand for gasoline blending.
